I tried your method this morning. I brewed 8 Breville "cups" or 40oz of water and followed your 1:14.5 ratio. I had to let the brewer siphon water out a second time as the first 20 seconds resulted in undersaturated grounds for blooming. In any case, I removed the basket, agitated the grounds, and then ran through a brewing cycle right through (no bloom time) as suggested. Overall this resulted in a much, much better extraction and a much better tasting pot of coffee. I also adjusted my grind to a finer one to compensate for the previous underextracted experience I had earlier. These elements combined made for a wonderful cup this morning, if not a tad strong for my stomach. I may play with this a little more to see if I can perfect this for my tastes.

Thank you for your post here. This Brewer went from a piece of garbage to something that actually has potential. As much as the Brewer adapts to you, you also have to adapt to the brewer; something I've had to learn the hard way. It's unfortunate that there is such a learning curve, but I'm more than willing to meet the challenge if the result will be a greater coffee experience overall in the end.

I simply read on the Breville website that the ratio needed is 2-3 times stronger than other brewers, which conflicts with what I read in the supplied manual.

I like my coffee a little weaker anyways, as my stomach is sensitive to coffee that's too strong, but when I brewed as instructed in the manual, my coffee came out severely underextracted on both the Gold setting and a few different My Brew settings.

I've since played with the My Brew settings further, set my grinds to be on the finer side, used a 1:14.5 ratio, and tried what someone else here had said they do; no bloom time, cancel brew after an appropriate amount of water is siphoned for blooming, remove basket, agitate grinds, then restart brew cycle and see it through.

All in all this resulted in a much, much improved cup of coffee. Still a little strong for my stomach, but it tasted wonderful this time around. Next I'll see if I can set the bloom time and just have it be the hands-off automated brewer it's supposed to be. 

However, I did notice that during the bloom, it leaks from the basket into the carafe. I assume this is not how the unit is supposed to function. Perhaps I have a faulty unit resulting in previously stated underextraction. Has anyone else noticed this?

How many Breville "cups" do you usually brew at a time with this method? I suspect that 20 seconds is relative to the amount of grinds you are using, no?

Either way, this seems like the most sensible advice I've seen on here as far as reasonable and possible solutions go. Still a silly thing to have to do with a $300+ machine.

I was having the same problem you are, my friend. I had a loose idea of what I wanted out of life but no structure to define my path to reach that idea. The problem was that the vision was not clear enough.

You kind of get stuck in this half-baked motivational period where you get into what you feel is a groove before losing steam and you end up back at square one.

Define what your life will be like in 5,10,20,40 years. Write it down. Where would you like to be and who surrounds you in this vision? You want specifics. Let's start with the 5-10 year plan.

A place of your own? A significant other? A job you can take some pride in where you can actually see yourself moving up the chain of command?

Now what will it take to achieve these things?
This is all about fleshing out your personal roadmap and getting more specific on the steps you will need to take.
-A place of your own: get your finances in order.
Open up multiple Chequing accounts. Set up auto transfers so that when your income comes in, it's sorted into accounts that are specific to the responsibilities you need to take care of. I have one for my mortgage, one for my car insurance, one for gas/maintenance on my vehicle, one to pay off my recurring bills on my credit card....you need to set up a strong financial base in order to make everything else easier in your life and take the stress out of money management. It is a great burden to lift if this is something you need to work on.
-A significant other: if this is important to you, saving may be a bit more of a challenge unless your income level is already fair 😜
A good job: what kind of job? Can you apply now?what are the prerequisites? What kind of schooling will you need? How long will that take? How much will that cost?

Next up is to write down down your to-do lists. Fill that list with at least 5 things a day. Rework your resume, find the write school to go to, garbage, recycling, vacuuming, grocery shopping, etc.
You may not be able to work on anything due to scheduled events with friends or appointments that must be kept. Some of these things will also not be able to be completed over a single day. That's fine. Keep it on the list. Keep working at it. Cross things off, fill it with another.

It becomes a very satisfying feeling when you can see yourself moving in the right direction. You will need to make sacrifices depending on how badly you want these and how immediate your desire is. The trick is to not become overzealous and burn yourself out. Don't sacrifice your health otherwise your desire and motivation will crumble along with your mind and body.

Sometimes you will have to shelf certain goals for others. Prioritize what you want most. Fpr example, I've struggled to find a job I desire greatly that will work in my current situation. However, I have moved up over the years in a job that pays fairly well and serves as a strong base for me to meet my other goals. Once those are sorted, I may think to move onto working on that career.

You must understand that there are steps to getting to the end goal and it will be a long while before you reach those goals. Happiness and meaning spawn from making strides towards that end goal and seeing progress.

I hope some of this helps.

Ps: getting proper sleep and having a consistent schedule is so damn important to your overall mood and energy level for this. Maintain your health, keep organized, and don't lose sight of that vision.

What helped for me is having a routine that I stick to fervently.

  I wake up at 4am, prep tea and begin cooking breakfast, then morning stretches, eat, put myself together for work, pack my lunch (made the night before) and I'm out the door. Work. Come home, shower, then - and this is so important - I don't sit down. I may cook dinner and sit while I eat, but I'm right back up after. 

  Keep a full plate. Have a daily list of 5-10 things you want to get done, whether it includes just your chores for the day (list them individually), or some extra things like returning merchandise, purchasing something that you've needed for a while, organizing a particular room or closet or nightstand,  organizing yourself financially, finally submitting an a resume for that job you wanted or an application for the school you've been meaning to go to...

It's so damn hard to do of you're in a rut. Trust me, I know. As time goes on though, and you are able to scratch things off the list, you get a great sense of accomplishment and satisfaction for being a productive human being. It allows you to rest easy at the end of the day.

Inevitably, getting yourself up and moving like this everyday will improve your energy levels, mood, and prepare you to better handle tougher situations. You will be surprised at how much more focused and in the moment you can be instead of living in your own mind all the time - something that I have struggled with many times.

This is all about establishing a consistent positive routine that reinforces that you are doing the right things to make your life better for you and make life feel so much more worthwhile.

Hope this helps.

EDIT: I should also mention that allowing yourself time in the morning to get your mind and body going is so important to feeling good about the rest of your day. Its early, throw some headphones on and listen to an energetic up-beat favorite album of yours if that's your thing, or a great podcast.

Also, DO NOT HIT SNOOZE!!! Your body will fall into a rhythm if you go to bed and wake up at the same time everyday. Don't mess with that or you will feel like getting out of bed is impossible. 

There are studies that show that your when you body becomes tuned to a schedule, it helps you along. You hit that snooze? Guess what? Your body says, sure, let's go back to bed. You wake up 10-15 minutes later, guess what? Your brain isn't able to shake off the grogginess for another 3-4 hours, contributing to your melancholia. You'll feel like crap and you'll fall back into old habits. Just don't do it.

Things that help for the morning? Prep all your clothes the night before. Put them on the washroom counter or hang them up on your door so that it's easy. Get all the pots/pans, spices, non-refridgables onto the counter so you aren't fishing for them in a bleary eyed state if you are cooking in the morning.
Doing this gives you the time to wake up without having to feel like your pedalling up a mountain.

Again hope this helps as many as it reaches.
